title: The Crucifixion and Burial of Jesus
overview: Pilate, pressed by the chief priests, hands Jesus over to be crucified, and the writer tells of his death and burial with an eye on Scripture being fulfilled.

parts.label: Whipped and mocked (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Pilate had Jesus brutally whipped and let his soldiers mock him as a fake king, with a crown of thorns and a purple robe, the color of royalty. Showing the beaten man with "Here is the man!" was likely meant to win pity or to prove he was no threat.

parts.label: Pilate gives in (vv. 6-16)
parts.note: The leaders shift to a religious charge, that Jesus claimed to be God's Son, which unsettles Pilate, and Jesus tells him his power is only on loan from above. When they hint that freeing a rival "king" would make Pilate disloyal to the emperor, he gives way.

parts.label: The cross and the sign (vv. 17-24)
parts.note: Jesus was crucified just outside the city between two others, under a sign naming his "crime" in the region's three main languages, which Pilate refused to soften. The soldiers splitting his clothes and gambling for his seamless tunic is, for this writer, a line from Psalm 22 coming true.

parts.label: His mother and his death (vv. 25-30)
parts.note: Jesus places his mother and "the disciple whom he loved", who is never named here, in each other's care, and that disciple takes her into his home. His last words, "It is finished," are usually read to mean his work was complete, not only that his life was over.

parts.label: Legs and the spear (vv. 31-37)
parts.note: Breaking the legs sped up death, since the crucified could no longer push up to breathe, and the leaders wanted the bodies down before a holy Sabbath. The writer stresses that an eyewitness saw the spear wound, and Christians read the unbroken bones as linking Jesus to the Passover lamb, whose bones were not to be broken.

parts.label: A hurried burial (vv. 38-42)
parts.note: Joseph, a secret follower, and Nicodemus, who first came to Jesus by night, now step forward to bury him with a huge amount of spices, a quantity fit for someone greatly honored. They used a new tomb close by because the Sabbath was about to begin.

disagreement: Christians agree Jesus' death is central but differ on how it saves: as taking the punishment others deserved, as defeating evil and death, as a supreme example of self-giving love, or as some mix of these.
think: When someone in power knows what is right but gives way under pressure, how much of the blame do you think belongs to them?
